old: Start smaller:
new: Would you be able to start a bit smaller?

old: “Show me one body sensation.” “Show me one word.” “Show me whether today is for listening or resting.”
new: Show yourself one sensation in your body, one word, whether to listen or rest today etc?

old: First ask what feels fake: the wording, the image, the expectation, or the role you’re trying to perform. Not experiencing an inner voice or image isn’t, by itself, resistance or a missing adult capacity. Correct an explicitly unwanted invitation. If you recognize a protective part, you can talk to it:
new: Do you know what is fake about it? The words/image/what you are expecting/ the role? It might be that you just don’t have that ‘thing’ in your head (voice/image etc) yet. It isn’t because you don’t have a ‘thing’ in your head doing this that you don’t have this ‘grown up’ thing yet or that you are resisting doing this. If it feels like you are being asked to do something you don’t want to do, then correct this. It could be that you have a part that is trying to protect you from doing this, so talk to this part.

old: “What are you protecting me from?” “Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?” “Are you afraid this is performance?”
new: Maybe try asking it “what are you protecting me from?” Or “are you afraid that I am going to lie to myself again?” Or “are you afraid that this is going to be a performance?”

old: The voice may be the inherited parent enforcing an old belonging rule. Don’t argue with it. Ask which rule it is enforcing and what ordinary evidence would make the new adult voice more believable.
new: It could be that you have picked up an inner voice of a parent that is enforcing a rule that if you do this then you will belong. In this case, don’t argue with this part. Try and find out what rule it is enforcing and then try and find some ‘every day life’ evidence to support your new ‘grown up’ voice.

old: The fake feeling can also mean that a needed adult capacity isn’t available yet. Stop demanding a convincing voice. If you can already observe what is happening, borrow the particular warmth, boundary, or direction you lack. A real or imagined caring figure can help. Try one believable sentence or action and see how it is received.
new: If it feels like you are picking up that you don’t have this ‘thing’ in your head yet, that tells you that you shouldn’t try and believe what this ‘thing’ (inner voice) is saying yet. As long as you have some ‘observing ego’ to do this work, you can borrow what you need from someone that you know has got this ‘thing’ (warmth, boundaries, direction etc). It could be a family member, friend, famous person etc. Try something out that rings true for you, it could be a sentence, action etc and see how it goes.

old: Intensity then gets mistaken for meaning. Sometimes the inner child is finally speaking. Sometimes a Protector is showing fear, or shame, grief, anger, longing, and other buried material are asking for care. But an intense state can also be bodily overload, environmental chaos, sleep deprivation, or plain confusion. A frightening image isn’t automatically truth, a bad feeling isn’t automatically a lesson, and a “download” doesn’t deserve belief merely because it came with excellent lighting.
new: It can be useful to notice that a certain state of intensity may have meaning: perhaps it is a way of connecting with inner child parts, or a Protector who is afraid, or other parts who feel shame/grief/anger/longing etc. It can also be that the body is overloaded, the environment is chaotic, there’s a sleep deficit or there’s confusion about something. But just because something appears in a vivid image, or feels bad, or happens to be in the right light for a ‘download’, doesn’t mean it’s true.

old: Before trying to interpret the state, ask a simpler question:
new: Before looking for the meaning of a state, it’s important to ask:

old: Read this slowly into a recorder, speak it aloud, or learn its movement and use silent words if that comes easily. Choose one anchor—a sound, bodily contact, or your two-hand practice—and an opening phrase. Keep using the same anchor where the words refer to it. Pause between paragraphs; don’t read the delivery directions aloud.
new: This is intended to be read slowly into a recorder, or read aloud to you, or learned and used as silent words. You will need to choose one of the three anchors (sound, bodily contact or two hands etc.), and stick with it throughout. You may want to choose an opening phrase to say as well. Whenever ‘the anchor’ is referred to use the one you have chosen. Pause for a few moments at the end of each paragraph. Do not read aloud the instructions for how to read.

old: Let your eyes settle somewhere in the room, somewhere they can rest for a little while, and notice the difference between looking for something and letting what is already there come into view.
new: Can you notice where your eyes are settling in the room?

old: There is a surface beneath you. Notice where you meet it … the contact, the pressure, whatever you can actually feel. And while you notice that, a sound may reach you, or a breath may draw your attention, without needing you to arrange either one.
new: As you notice the surface that you are sitting or lying on, can you also notice what it feels like to be in contact with that surface? And as you notice the surface, can you also notice the anchor?

old: You can give this a little time.
new: Is there time to do this?

old: A thought about the day may still be here. A thought about whether you’re doing this properly may be here too. There is room to notice a thought and return to the anchor you chose, without finishing the thought first.
new: Is there a thought there about something that’s happened today? Is there a thought about how to do this? Whatever is there, can you turn your attention to the anchor? Even if there is a thought there, can you turn your attention to the anchor?

old: And as you return, you may find one detail that holds your interest … something about the sound, or the contact, or that particular way of listening … and let attention stay with it long enough to become curious.
new: Things to consider when you return: Is there something that captured your attention? Sound, touch, listening?

old: Perhaps you can give yourself the time you would give someone you care about who has begun to speak and hasn’t yet found the words. You can remain nearby, listening, without finishing their sentence for them.
new: Will you give as much time to someone you care about, who’s speaking to you?

old: Let your chosen phrase come to mind now. Say it as an invitation, and notice how it is received.
new: How was it to use the phrase you selected?

old: As you continue, your eyes can close, soften, or stay open. Let that be a choice you make. Listening may deepen while a sound from the room remains available in the background.
new: Consider closing your eyes, softening your eyes, or keep them open as you go through this. Notice the difference it may make as you listen to what’s in the room around you, allowing it to be in the background.

old: Count slowly from five to one. Give each number its own moment.
new: Begin by slowly counting down from 5 to 1.

old: Five. Notice your chosen anchor again. Four. Let attention gather around what you find. Three. Leave a little space after the words. Two. Listen into that space, without preparing an answer. One. Stay here for a moment.
new: 5 Perhaps, once again you may want to notice what you have chosen to use as your anchor 4 3 2 1

old: Bring your chosen concern lightly to mind, or remain with your wish for contact. Let it be present without rehearsing its whole story.
new: Bring to mind something you would like to bring to mind or just your wish to contact it

old: What am I noticing now?
new: Perhaps you can begin to notice what you are noticing

old: Give the response time to take its own form. It might be a sensation, a few words, an image, a feeling, or an impulse to move. There may be nothing clear yet.
new: Perhaps you can allow yourself some time to notice what you are noticing whether it is sensations, words, images, feelings, movements or something else entirely

old: Leave room to notice, with words or without them.
new: Perhaps you can allow yourself some time to notice this with or without words

old: Reverse whatever you used to enter. If you floated, regain chosen weight. If you became small, return to ordinary scale. If you met a younger state or several parts, confirm present wholeness, body ownership, and adult judgment. If you traveled, come back by the same route. Keep only the qualities you deliberately chose.
new: Bring yourself out of the session, in reverse order of how you got into it. If you floated up, float back down again, etc., remembering that you have whatever weight you chose earlier in the session. If you shrank yourself, grow back to your normal size. If you went back to when you were younger or went inside to talk to parts of yourself, remember that you are now a whole person, this is your body, and you're using your adult judgement now. If you traveled somewhere, come back in the same way that you went, remembering to bring back only that which you chose to bring back.

old: “I bring back only what is useful now. The rest can remain safely held until there is more capacity. I return to the room, the body, the day, and one honest action. All instructions to deepen or remain in this session are finished. I keep only the ordinary-life intention or future-practice cue I consciously chose; neither keeps today’s altered state running. I am myself, in my body, with adult judgment fully available.”
new: Say to yourself, "I am bringing back only that which will be of use to me now. Everything else will remain safely stored until such time as I choose to use it. I am now coming back to this place, to my body, to normal living, to one honest action at a time. From this point on, nothing will make me go inside again unless I choose to use these practices again in the future."

old: One — feel the body’s contact and chosen weight. Two — let the breath return to its ordinary rhythm. Three — hear the room and name where you are. Four — move fingers, toes, shoulders, and eyes. Five — eyes open, present, ordinary, clear. The session has ended.
new: Count yourself out of the session: "One, coming back into your body, remembering that you have whatever weight you chose at the beginning of the session. Two, coming back to normal breathing. Three, becoming aware of all the sounds around you now, and where you are. Four, moving your fingers, your toes, your shoulders, your eyes. Five, opening your eyes, feeling normal, the session is now over."

old: Name the day or date. Look left, right, near, and far. Move before standing, and stand only when steady. Check that you are actually oriented and alert; repeating the count is not proof of a complete return. Note only what actually appeared, and any action it calls for. Then do something normal.
new: Whether coming out of an induction by a live person or from an audio recording, once you are told or instructed to open your eyes, you may want to enhance your coming out by saying to yourself either what day it is or what date it is, looking to your left and right, looking at something close and something far away, moving a bit before standing up. Once you feel steady, stand up. Make sure you are oriented and alert. Just because you can count does not mean you are oriented and alert. Mentally make note of any information that came up during the session and if there is something that you need or do not need to do as a result of the session. Then proceed to do whatever it is that you normally do.

old: If a recording stops unexpectedly: say, “The recording stopped and the session is over.” Open your eyes, name the location and day, press your feet or hands into a surface, move, look around, and use the five-step count. Don’t wait for the missing narrator to release you.
new: In the event that you are using a recording and for some reason it stops, just say to yourself that the recording has stopped and the session is over. Then use the above method to come out by opening your eyes, saying where you are, saying what day it is, pushing down with your feet or hands, moving about, looking about and then using the 5 step method listed above.

old: Sleep is separate. A sleep recording may end in sleep or quiet rest. A waking recording shouldn’t end by preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, an undefined reset word, or an invitation to remain altered indefinitely.
new: NOTE: When using a recording to take you into a sleep state, it is fine to let the recording put you to sleep or into a quiet time of resting. But when using a recording during a waking practice, the recording should not be leaving you in a role, with lowered judgement, with lowered movement capabilities, blank, with an un-defined “reset word” or inviting you to stay in an altered state for an unlimited amount of time.
